steps.text: Edit a canvas file through the Canvas MCP
Start the server
`Client` spawns `codecaine-canvas mcp` over stdio
`cli.ts` resolves the workspace directory
`mcp.ts` sends the instructions string at initialize
Open a canvas
`Client` calls `canvas_open` with a canvas id
`openCanvasFile` reads, validates, and hashes the file
Build the draft and inject a page frame
The frame is added only when the board has no root section.
The injected frame stays in the draft and is never written.
Resolve the whole board as the scope
Seed the lint baseline and sync the request queue
Return the description, digest, lint findings, and file hash
Apply one edit
`Client` calls one toolkit tool
`callToolkitTool` validates the arguments against the agent's schema
Run the operation or workflow tool on the draft
Skip the save when the draft did not change
Errors, no-ops, and `look` leave the draft untouched.
Persist the edit
`persistCanvasFile` re-reads the file and compares its hash
Refuse the save when the hash differs
The session stays conflicted until `canvas_open` runs again.
Diff the last persisted document against the draft
Replay the diff through `canvas.applyAgentPatch`
Validate the result and write it atomically
Advance the stored hash and the persisted base
Return the tool result with a `SAVED` line
Repeat apply and persist until the client disconnects

The guard is the sha256 of the file bytes as the session last read or wrote them. A different hash at save time means another writer saved the file: Studio, a text editor, or git. The server never overwrites that change and never merges.

Studio guards the opposite direction with its own revision check and reloads an open board when the server writes it. That behavior belongs to Persistence and embedding.

Relation to the Kernel Agent and the Docs MCP

Three agent-facing paths edit canvas documents. The kernel agent path and the Canvas MCP share one toolkit and differ in the lifecycle around it. The Docs MCP is a separate tool set for canvases embedded in documentation.
